business_problem: Dongwha Enterprise needed a more resilient platform for fast-growing smart-factory sensor and business data after relational databases and later self-managed MongoDB infrastructure created failures, inconsistent queries, and operational overhead.
solution_summary: Dongwha Enterprise built its D-FactoryIn smart-factory platform to collect, analyze, and operationalize production data in real time, but the original relational database could not keep up as factory telemetry expanded. After first moving to MongoDB Community Edition on Amazon EC2 to escape read/write bottlenecks, the company still faced monitoring, optimization, and version-control burdens as more factories came online. MongoDB Atlas became the next step because it combined MongoDB's document model with native time-series support and managed operations. Atlas now stores facility and business data for smart-factory workloads, supports automatic index recommendations for slow-query analysis, simplifies scaling, and provides alerts for cluster, disk, and network conditions. This let Dongwha keep engineers focused on Industry 4.0 applications while tracing defective products, analyzing processes, and expanding service coverage across factories.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Atlas
solution_components.role: Stores Dongwha's smart-factory facility and business data while providing time-series support, monitoring, and managed operations.

data_flow: Sensor and business data from Dongwha's smart factories flow into the D-FactoryIn platform on MongoDB Atlas, where time-series storage and indexing support real-time analysis, defect tracing, and business-friendly insight generation. Atlas monitoring and alerts then feed operators information about cluster, disk, and network health.
business_outcome: Dongwha improved retrieval performance, reduced hardware and administration issues, and scaled its smart-factory platform across multiple sites while giving engineers more time to focus on digital manufacturing use cases.
metrics: Dongwha Enterprise now operates facility management services with MongoDB Atlas across five smart factories at home and abroad.
